offence_severity: Death caused by an axe and a gun, punishable under Section 302 IPC
physical_harm: Injuries on the dead body caused by an axe and a gun
key_evidence_accepted: The evidence of PW-13 is corroborated by the evidence of PW-6, the Investigating Officer (PW-19), and the inquest report (Ext. P-2), which show injuries on the deceased caused by an axe and a gun, and the recovery of the axe handle.
witness_credibility: The court found PW-13's evidence reliable despite discrepancies, noting that normal discrepancies in witness accounts are expected and do not automatically cast doubt on credibility unless they are material.
post_offence_conduct: PW-13 ran away from the place of occurrence due to fear of the appellants who had threatened him, but this was explained as a result of his fear and not as an indication of unreliability.
trial_duration: Offence: 09.10.1998; Trial judgment: 08.06.2005; High Court decision: 08.06.2005; Supreme Court decision: 19.03.2013
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused: Lalit Chauhan, Somanadri Goud, Kshatrashal Raj, Abhishek Vinod Deshmukh (for Parekh & Co.); Counsel for the State: Ritu Raj Biswas, Gopal Singh
investigation_status: FIR registered, charge sheet filed, trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Conviction upheld; High Court: Conviction upheld; Supreme Court: Appeal of appellant No.2 allowed, appeal of appellant No.1 dismissed
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the accused were guilty of the offence under Section 302/34 IPC, supported by the testimony of an eye-witness, PW-13, and corroborated by other evidence such as the recovery of the weapon and the inquest report. They also contended that the motive to kill was not established, but argued that direct evidence of the offence was sufficient.
defence_argument: The defence argued that appellant No.2 was below 18 years of age at the time of the offence and thus a juvenile under the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2000, and that the 2000 Act should apply. They also claimed that the conviction of appellant No.1 was based on an unreliable sole witness, PW-13, who had run away from the scene and was a suspect, and that there were discrepancies in the evidence, lack of weapon recovery, and no established motive.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2000, applies to offences committed prior to its commencement if the accused was below 18 years of age at the time of the offence. It also emphasized that discrepancies in witness accounts are not sufficient to discard evidence unless they are 'material discrepancies' creating reasonable doubt.
precedent_relied_upon: Hari Ram v. State of Rajasthan and Anr. (2009) 13 SCC 211; State of Rajasthan v. Smt. Kalki and Anr. (1981) 2 SCC 752; Badri v. State of Rajasthan (1976) 1 SCC 442; Lallu Manjhi and Anr. v. State of Jharkhand AIR 2003 SC 854; Suresh Chandra Bahri v. State of Bihar AIR 1994 SC 2420
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed based on the conviction that the accused were guilty of the offence under Section 302/34 IPC, with the court upholding the trial court's and High Court's conviction and sentence for appellant No.1, while remitting the case of appellant No.2 to the Juvenile Justice Board.
other_sentence_order: The case of appellant No.2 was remitted to the Juvenile Justice Board of North Tripura district for disposal in accordance with the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2000.
